record.title: Recursive video retrieval reports higher frozen-VLA success on perturbed simulation tasks
record.summary: A 5 October 2026 preprint reports Recursive Video In-Context Learning (RV-ICL), which indexes one task demonstration into four read-only levels—keyframes, phases, moments and short clips—and lets a planner retrieve detail for its current subgoal. The authors report HarnessVLA success rising from 92.6% to 96.5% on LIBERO-PRO and 86.7% to 95.8% on LIBERO-Plus. These are author-reported simulation results: on LIBERO-PRO the RV-ICL arm used 50 episodes while prior-work baselines used 100, and the paper’s reported significance statistic does not yet have a recovered matched-data audit. On LIBERO-Plus the methods were compared on a stratified 120 of 10,030 variants. The paper reports 1.8x wall-clock time and 1.4x input tokens on that comparison; physical-robot transfer is untested.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors propose a four-level, read-only hierarchy over one demonstration per base task, with clips retrieved as the planner reaches relevant subgoals.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In author-reported simulation results, HarnessVLA success rises from 92.6% to 96.5% on LIBERO-PRO and from 86.7% to 95.8% on LIBERO-Plus.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: LIBERO-PRO compares 50 RV-ICL episodes per cell with 100 prior-work baseline episodes; LIBERO-Plus evaluates a stratified 120 of 10,030 variants, with 17–18 cases per perturbation dimension.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper reports 1.8x wall-clock time and 1.4x input tokens versus HarnessVLA on the LIBERO-Plus subset; all experiments are in simulation and use one robot and one VLA.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The reported improvement does not establish transfer to physical robots or broad task distributions, and the main LIBERO-PRO baseline comparison is not matched episode by episode.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched-seed replication or recovered per-episode RV-ICL results and exact seed list; the paper’s aggregate significance statistic is not independently auditable.
Physical-robot transfer and performance across other VLA models, robots and task families remain unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported improvement transfers under matched trials, retrieving demonstration video only at relevant subgoals could materially improve long-horizon manipulation without retraining the VLA. The evidence is one author-reported simulation paper with unequal sample counts for its main baseline comparison, small perturbation cells and a latency/token cost, so the consequence is notable but conditional.
limitations: The main LIBERO-PRO baseline values are reported from prior work with 100 episodes per cell; RV-ICL uses 50, so the comparison is not same-run or episode-matched.

Authors report z=2.97, p=0.003 for the aggregate LIBERO-PRO comparison, but exact per-task/seed outcomes, seed overlap and test code were not recovered; aggregate-count recomputation and dependence handling remain open.
LIBERO-Plus uses a stratified 120 of 10,030 variants, with only 17–18 examples per perturbation dimension.
The reported LIBERO-Plus success change costs 1.8x wall-clock time and 1.4x input tokens relative to HarnessVLA.
All experiments are simulated, use one robot and one VLA, and do not establish performance on physical robots or other embodiments.
Demonstrations are assumed to expose task sub-events; tasks lacking gripper/fixture event signals need other segmentation methods.
brief.summary: A 5 October 2026 preprint reports Recursive Video In-Context Learning (RV-ICL), which indexes one task demonstration into four read-only levels—keyframes, phases, moments and short clips—and lets a planner retrieve detail for its current subgoal. The authors report HarnessVLA success rising from 92.6% to 96.5% on LIBERO-PRO and 86.7% to 95.8% on LIBERO-Plus. These are author-reported simulation results: on LIBERO-PRO the RV-ICL arm used 50 episodes while prior-work baselines used 100, and the paper’s reported significance statistic does not yet have a recovered matched-data audit. On LIBERO-Plus the methods were compared on a stratified 120 of 10,030 variants. The paper reports 1.8x wall-clock time and 1.4x input tokens on that comparison; physical-robot transfer is untested.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that recursive, subgoal-specific video retrieval improves a frozen-VLA agent across perturbed simulation benchmarks and carries to a second planner. No independent replication or physical-robot outcome was established.
technical.compute_or_cost: On the LIBERO-Plus subset, authors report 1.8x wall-clock time and 1.4x input tokens versus HarnessVLA. Video preparation/storage and deployment economics were not established.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors report HarnessVLA success increasing from 92.6% to 96.5% on LIBERO-PRO and 86.7% to 95.8% on LIBERO-Plus. LIBERO-PRO RV-ICL results aggregate 50 episodes per cell versus 100 for prior-work baselines. LIBERO-Plus uses a stratified subset of 120 from 10,030 variants, with 17–18 cases per perturbation dimension. The paper reports 1.8x wall-clock time and 1.4x input tokens versus HarnessVLA on the LIBERO-Plus subset.
technical.implementation_status: Authors link a public code repository and describe a runnable pipeline; the research desk did not run or independently audit it in this activation.
technical.mechanism: RV-ICL segments one demonstration per base task at task sub-events and exposes a four-level hierarchy—event keyframes, phases, moments and short video clips—through read-only tools. The planner first reads coarse levels and can retrieve a clip for the current subgoal during execution, subject to a viewing budget.
technical.novelty: Treat a demonstration as a hierarchical, queryable memory that the planner revisits when a subgoal needs visual detail, rather than providing the full video or fixed keyframes up front.
technical.regime: One demonstration per base task; GPT-6 Astra planner orchestrating a frozen pi0.5 primitive through RPent/HarnessVLA; LIBERO-PRO and a stratified LIBERO-Plus simulation subset. No other robot embodiment, physical deployment or broad task distribution was evaluated.
technical.reproducibility: Paper reports its sample counts and configurations, but exact per-episode outcomes, exact seed IDs and statistical code were not recovered. The main LIBERO-PRO comparison uses a prior-work baseline with a different episode count.
technical.strongest_baseline: HarnessVLA with the same frozen pi0.5 primitive. On LIBERO-PRO, the baseline values are from prior work and use twice as many episodes per cell; on the paper’s stratified LIBERO-Plus subset, the authors run both methods in the same time window.

brief.title: Recursive video retrieval reports higher frozen-VLA success on perturbed simulation tasks
brief.why_it_matters: The hierarchy makes demonstration video an on-demand memory source: an agent sees task structure before planning and retrieves short clips near a grasp, release or other subgoal. If the reported gains survive matched testing, this could improve long-horizon manipulation without retraining the VLA. Current evidence is limited to one author-run simulation study with unequal LIBERO-PRO sample counts, small perturbation cells and a measurable latency/token cost.
